subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Should maintainers require current-main live measurement before changing active embedded-run transcript persistence, or sponsor an async/off-thread `SessionManager` refactor now based on source evidence?
rationale: The source-backed sync I/O path is real, but the observed abort chain has not been reproduced against current main and the safest implementation crosses core session persistence invariants.

options.title: Require measurement first
options.body: Keep this open for a controlled current-main run that records `eventLoopDelayMaxMs`, transcript write size, and any stale-session recovery outcome before changing persistence semantics.

options.title: Sponsor async persistence design
options.body: Approve owner-led work to move active `SessionManager` writes off synchronous JSONL I/O now, with broad session/cache/repair tests and performance proof.

options.title: Treat caps and liveness work as enough
options.body: Defer transcript persistence changes unless a fresh repro shows the remaining capped payload path still causes false liveness recovery.

recommendation.title: Require measurement first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a controlled current-main run that records `eventLoopDelayMaxMs`, transcript write size, and any stale-session recovery outcome before changing persistence semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily in the transcript writer/session-accessor boundary that jalehman recently worked on.
